hypotheses.claim: The facts the languages write (relation columns) are kept file after file until the project phase.
hypotheses.evidence: dump 471: 172 MB of facts columns in 126 + 134 allocations, the 9 workers' columns, cleared per file (FactsWorker::release) with their capacity kept; 4 MB of them at dump 474 after the workers are dropped

hypotheses.claim: The parsed models (element tables, names) of the files read are kept until the project phase.
hypotheses.evidence: the element table is 617 MB at dump 471 in exactly 9 allocations per column (one table per worker, reused), and 0 MB at dump 474; names 129 -> 16 MB

hypotheses.claim: Each worker keeps the capacity its largest file needed, so 9 workers x the largest file's tables set the file-phase peak.
hypotheses.evidence: avg 7.05 MB per element column per worker, 6.4 MB file buffer per worker; without the 27 files over 1 MB the worker tables at the file phase's end fall from 981 MB (element 617, facts 172, names 129, bytes 63) to 217 MB (103, 51, 56, 7) and the file-phase end from 2288 to 1516 MB (-772 MB). The project phase is unchanged (4286 MB peak heap)

hypotheses.claim: The tables are large because a file's tree is built whether or not a rule governing the file reads its language's relations.
hypotheses.evidence: with only program-implementation-boundary placed (it governs Rust sources) the worker tables still reach 1059 MB (element 669, facts 179, names 140, bytes 71) at that run's peak; LanguageAdapter::read parses every recognized file with the run-wide `wanted` (core outbound/language/adapters/use_case/adapter.rs:236). Which rules govern each large JSON file was not listed

question_1_what_holds_it.answer: At dcea2ee7df the file phase ends at 2288 MB of heap (project-retention measured 2513 MB on 8a59189be5, a different tree). 981 MB is the 9 workers' reused tables. 760 MB is per-file outputs kept for the end of the run: 346 MB of answer rows, 252 MB of the store's copy of the same rows, and 161 MB of handed metadata, text and notes. 164 MB is the spill index and the pending spill bytes. 122 MB is tm, and 252 MB is other engine state (name arenas, glob hits, the program).

owners.worker tables (981 MB): core domain/workers/types.rs Tables.elements, .symbols, .bytes and the FactsWorker columns, owned by each worker for the whole file phase
owners.answer rows (346 MB): core outbound/row_sink/adapters/collect (the SDK's collected LintReport rows)
owners.store records (413 MB): core Tables.fresh: Vec<FreshRecord> -> Record.outcome Ran {rows, handed}, written by finish_run

question_2_needed_or_accident.needed_by_project_phase: the spill index (145 MB), though not at its size: it holds about 1.5-2 million stretches, each with a 48-byte FrontierProof clone that is constant per bucket except its coverage; the workers' name arenas (38 MB, finish/service.rs:206), which the frontier words point into; and the program and plan
question_2_needed_or_accident.needed_later_not_by_project_phase: the answer rows (346 MB, handed to tm after the run) and the store records (413 MB, written at finish_run). Both live from the file phase through the project peak only because the engine keeps them in memory until the run ends
question_2_needed_or_accident.accident: the worker tables' capacity (981 MB), kept at the largest file's size by all 9 workers and released only when the file phase ends (that sets the file-phase peak, not the project phase's); the second copy of the findings rows (252 MB); handed metadata kept in memory after the words were already staged (161 MB); and the per-stretch proof copy (about 100 MB of the spill index)

question_3_floor_or_fixable.answer: Mostly fixable in place. Only the per-(rule, file) frontier metadata (spill index plus handed buckets, 252 MB) is the fact model's per-tree floor in its count, the counterpart of the Django study's ~378 MB of facts. Even its bytes per entry can shrink.

question_4_guard.floor: With l1 and l3 under the current model, the project phase's floor is the residual it cannot drop plus the largest rule's materialized capture. That residual is tm's plan (122-186 MB), the answer rows in their most compact form (about 250 MB), the name arenas (38 MB), a compact spill index (about 50 MB), the decoded frontier at project start (96 MB) and the program (about 100 MB): about 650-700 MB. Adding 685 MB gives about 1.35 GB of heap, or about 1.45 GB RSS. The file phase can reach the guard; the project phase cannot while program-implementation-boundary's and shared-walk-owner's path-split captures (local-dependencies has 3,480,084 rows) are published whole. Getting under 1.33 GB needs project-retention l2 (stream those captures) on top of l1 and l3, or a different guard

levers.lever: Bound the worker tables. After a file whose element table, facts columns, names or byte buffer grew past a cap, a worker shrinks them back to the cap instead of keeping the largest file's capacity. Files over a size bound are read one at a time, so 9 workers never hold 9 large trees at once. Alternative, needing a semantic check first (h4): skip building the tree for a file whose governing rules read none of its language's relations. That check must keep the unread/partial reporting of a file that fails to parse byte-identical. Scheduling and buffer lifetime only; no second data structure.
levers.size: core application/file_analysis (Worker tables, release after the visit) and the scheduler's admission, about 80-200 lines; the h4 variant adds a per-file wanted set from the mask, about 150-300 lines
levers.evidence: h3: 981 MB of worker tables at dump 471, 9 allocations per column; the ablation without the 27 files over 1 MB lowers the file-phase end by 772 MB

levers.lever: Keep one copy of the findings rows. stage_outcome already moves each fresh record's bucket words into the store's staging spool; move Ran.rows (FindingRows) there the same way, so the store's copy is not held in memory until finish_run.

levers.lever: Stage the handed metadata too: Handed.buckets' proofs and handles, Handed.text and Handed.notes go to the same spool as the words, not into the in-memory FreshRecord.
levers.size: same mechanism as l3b, about 100-200 lines
